source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Work on Attention Layer Outputs
source.authors: Connor Kissane; robertzk; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Specialisation and polysemanticity of induction heads; token-specific feature decomposition

record.tranche_reason: The post investigates induction-like behavior and its upstream circuit using SAE feature attribution and activation patching in a two-layer model, rather than reproducing the original training-time measurements.
record.gate_note: The post does not measure training-time formation, an in-context-learning loss-by-token-index gain, or a training-loss bump. It also does not test induction across model families or few-shot task learning. Its rows concern induction-feature behavior, attribution, patching, and induction-head ablation.
record.test_reason: The post's main goal is validating attention-output SAEs, but it reports circuit evidence for the induction mechanism. This is a new setting: gelu-2l, a two-layer model with MLPs, not attention-only. Induction head L1H6 computes 'B is next' features by attending to and copying the B token. A layer-0 previous-token head (L0H2) is necessary in a patched example. Mean-ablating L1H6 turns off nearly all induction-behaving features.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that SAEs on attention outputs (hook_z) yield sparse, interpretable features, with ~82% of living features interpretable. The induction-feature family (~5% of living features) is computed mainly by induction head L1H6, with a previous-token head upstream. They also report L1H6 polysemanticity and caution that their proxies and heuristics are crude.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE feature attribution, a behavioral heuristic, head ablation, and activation patching to investigate induction-related circuitry; it does not reproduce the original training-time phase-change or in-context-learning measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The board-feature proxy misses some valid induction-pattern examples; the authors also report false positives at lower feature-activation ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: Induction head L1H6 is polysemantic: it also supports non-induction code-completion features (6693, 4635, 12200). Mean-ablating it raises loss on those tokens far more than ablating control head L1H0.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads also carry non-induction functions (attention head polysemanticity).

fits_no_version.finding: A large 'one feature per suffix token' family of induction SAE features (~5% of living features) is computed by a single induction head.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction head output decomposes into many token-specific induction features under SAEs.

record.problems: Evidence centers on one two-layer model with MLPs and one detailed board-induction feature. The authors describe their automatic feature-selection and behavior heuristics as crude and likely to have false positives and false negatives; the proxy has a reported correlation of 0.50. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The post also reports non-induction code-completion features associated with L1H6 and their loss changes under head ablation. These concern head polysemanticity rather than any listed claim version, so they were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: Attention-only transformers (gelu-2l has MLPs). Composition is shown in only one patched example, with no rigorous reverse-engineering of the full upstream circuit (authors' own caveat). Formation of the head is not studied.
All: no training-time dynamics, ICL gain or loss bump.
All: no ICL-by-token-index measure, no large models.
All: no variation of data or training.

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly an SAE-methods post; its induction evidence is a by-product case study in one model with MLPs. The proxy-correlation and downstream-loss rows (r1–r5) describe SAE feature quality, so they are relinked to none and the reader's limits_scope label based on r1–r2 is dropped. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests an induction feature and its circuit in one two-layer language model with MLPs, not an attention-only transformer. It does not establish the full mechanism across models.
No training-time formation window, in-context-learning gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
Does not measure most in-context learning or loss falling with token index in large transformers.
Only one model is studied; no model-family, size, training-run, architecture, or modality sweep.
No comparison of data properties or training setups for induction formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanism with induction heads.
Does not track formation over training or test whether formation comprises separate transitions.

rows.subject: gelu-2l
rows.operation_detail: Compared the board-induction feature activation with a proxy for strict and fuzzy board induction.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between feature activity and the binary proxy
rows.locator: Feature Deep Dives, Induction Feature: Board induction, Specificity / Sensitivity Analysis
rows.note: The proxy is described as imperfect, including missed fuzzy-induction cases.
rows.check: Measures how well an SAE feature matches a hand-built proxy (r=0.50). This is SAE feature quality, not whether an induction head implements [A][B]…[A]→[B].

rows.subject: gelu-2l
rows.operation_detail: Manually checked proxy-negative examples satisfying the board-induction pattern.
rows.measure: False negatives found by the proxy
rows.locator: Feature Deep Dives, Induction Feature: Board induction, Specificity / Sensitivity Analysis
rows.note: The authors say these cases technically match the pattern but ‘board’ should not be predicted.
rows.check: Count of proxy false negatives (68) that the authors judge should not predict 'board'. This validates the proxy/feature, not the head mechanism.

rows.subject: gelu-2l
rows.operation_detail: Ablated feature 14 and measured per-token loss changes.
rows.measure: Share of total loss increase accounted for by tokens whose correct next token is ‘board’
rows.locator: Feature Deep Dives, Induction Feature: Board induction, Analyzing Downstream Effects
rows.note: Ablating the feature increased loss, mostly on board-prediction tokens.
rows.check: Downstream loss share from ablating the SAE feature (82%). This concerns the feature's use, not the induction head's mechanism or its composition.

rows.subject: gelu-2l
rows.operation_detail: Ablated feature 14's direct path to logits and measured per-token loss changes.
rows.measure: Share of total loss increase accounted for by board predictions
rows.locator: Feature Deep Dives, Induction Feature: Board induction, Analyzing Downstream Effects
rows.note: The direct path is reported as more important than the path through MLP1.
rows.check: Path-patching share for the feature's direct path (84%). This is about the feature's downstream route, not V1.

rows.subject: gelu-2l
rows.operation_detail: Ablated feature 14's path to mlp_in and measured per-token loss changes.
rows.measure: Share of total loss increase accounted for by board predictions
rows.locator: Feature Deep Dives, Induction Feature: Board induction, Analyzing Downstream Effects
rows.note: The authors report this path as less important than the feature's direct path to logits.
rows.check: The 55% share via mlp_in describes the feature's use through MLP1. 'Partial' has no meaning relative to V1.

relationships.condition: gelu-2l (two-layer, with MLPs), layer-1 induction head L1H6 and its 'B is next by induction' SAE features
relationships.reason: L1H6 shows induction attention on repeated random tokens (r7). It dominates the board feature's attribution (r6) and copies and attends to 'board' source tokens (r8, r9). The previous-token head L0H2 is necessary for the feature (r10). 450/586 L1H6-attributed features pass the induction heuristic vs 3/500 controls (r11, r12). Ablating L1H6 turns off 443/450 of them (r13).
relationships.display_finding: L1H6 attended to and copied earlier 'board' tokens and dominated the board feature's attribution, while that feature required previous-token head L0H2; the induction heuristic identified 450/586 features versus 3/500 controls, and ablating L1H6 disabled 443/450 identified features.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: gelu-2l (two-layer, with MLPs), layer-1 induction head L1H6 and its 'B is next by induction' SAE features
labels.reason: V1 explicitly concerns small attention-only transformers; gelu-2l has MLPs. Rows r6–r13 provide related mechanism evidence in this different setting, but do not test V1 as written. This untested scope is neither limits_scope nor challenges.

relation.reason: It measures induction behavior, source-token attribution, upstream necessity and head-ablation effects, rather than reporting only SAE performance.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own induction-behavior and circuit results in a two-layer model with MLPs, extending the setting and bearing on V4's architecture coverage.

source_check.notes: The synthesis explicitly acknowledges the MLP-model scope difference, and its study-specific facts are accurate. Upstream patching uses one example pair, does not fully reverse engineer composition, and the feature heuristics have acknowledged false positives and negatives.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The board-induction feature and the heuristically identified induction-feature family in gelu-2l
reader_labels.reason: The feature is attributed chiefly to an induction head, board tokens, and a previous-token head; the induction heuristic separates selected features from controls and head ablation turns off most selected features (r6–r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The feature-proxy correlation is 0.50 and the proxy has 68 manually checked false negatives, so the behavioral correspondence is not complete (r1–r2).
